general_rules: Extension content must remain anchored to the original model.
At least one core identifier or clearly core concept should appear in every extension answer.
Do not present extension identifiers as original source-code elements unless they are in the core invariant.
Prefer minimal coherent extensions over broad redesigns.
Extensions should remain tied to grievance, activation, policing, diffusion, or scaling in the rebellion setting.

families.name: state_refinement
rules: Must be presented as replacing or refining the original binary `active?` logic.
Must not be described as already present in the base source code.

families.name: network_layer
rules: Must be framed as an added interaction layer beyond local `neighborhood` dynamics.
Should remain connected to grievance, threshold effects, or activation.

families.name: broadcast_media
rules: Must be framed as an added global influence on grievance or activation.
Must not imply that broadcast media exists in the original code.

families.name: long_range_links
rules: Must be framed as adding nonlocal ties beyond the base spatial-local mechanism.
Should remain about rebellion spread, tipping, or cluster growth.

families.name: large_scale_optimization
rules: Must be presented as a scaling or implementation extension.
Should distinguish computational speed from rebellion dynamics.

families.name: early_warning_metrics
rules: Metrics may be added for analysis even if they are not part of the original code.
Should be tied to core quantities like `active?`, `grievance`, `vision`, or `government-legitimacy`.

general_rules: Extensions should remain tied to shepherd movement, searching, local sheep conditions, carrying behavior, or efficiency measurement.

families.name: state_refinement
rules: Must be framed explicitly as an extension beyond the original source model.
Must not claim these states already exist in the base code.

families.name: measurement_extension
rules: Added metrics must be framed as analytical extensions rather than built-in variables.
